audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Josiah covenant, religious purge, Passover, death at Megiddo, Jehoahaz removal, and Jehoiakim taxation narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for public scroll reading, covenant renewal, removal and destruction of sacred objects, qadesh terminology, women textile workers, Topheth and child protection, religious-site defilement, grave and bone desecration, execution of high-place priests, Passover, spirit-practitioner suppression, unmatched royal praise, unresolved collective wrath, Josiah's violent death, Egyptian imperial intervention, forced renaming, tribute, and taxation.

verses.restored: King sent, and they gathered to him all elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

modern.text: Then the king summoned all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּאַסְפ֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: King went up to house of YHWH, and with him every man of Judah, all inhabitants of Jerusalem, priests, prophets, and all people, from small to great. He read in their ears all words of scroll of covenant found in house of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the king went up into the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the LORD.

modern.text: And he went up to the house of the LORD with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, as well as the priests and the prophets—all the people small and great—and in their hearing he read all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בֵּית יְהוָ֡ה וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָה֩ וְכָל יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אִתּ֗וֹ וְהַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַנְּבִיאִ֔ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם לְמִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי֙ סֵ֣פֶר הַבְּרִ֔ית הַנִּמְצָ֖א בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: King stood by pillar and cut covenant before YHWH, to walk after YHWH and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all heart and all soul, to establish words of this covenant written in this scroll. All people stood in covenant.

familiar.text: And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

modern.text: So the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD to follow the LORD and to keep His commandments, decrees, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul, and to carry out the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people entered into the covenant. Josiah Destroys Idolatry (1 Kings 13:1–10; 2 Chronicles 34:3–7)

original.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ עַֽל הָ֨עַמּ֜וּד וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת אֶֽת הַבְּרִ֣ית לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה לָלֶ֜כֶת אַחַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ וְלִשְׁמֹ֨ר מִצְוֺתָ֜יו וְאֶת עֵדְוֺתָ֤יו וְאֶת חֻקֹּתָיו֙ בְּכָל לֵ֣ב וּבְכָל נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְהָקִ֗ים אֶת דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים עַל הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד כָּל הָעָ֖ם בַּבְּרִֽית

verses.restored: King commanded Hilkiah the high priest, priests of second rank, and guardians of threshold to bring from temple of YHWH all vessels made for Baal, Asherah, and all host of heavens. He burned them outside Jerusalem in fields of Kidron and carried their dust to Bethel.

familiar.text: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the LORD all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Bethel.

modern.text: Then the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests second in rank, and the doorkeepers to remove from the temple of the LORD all the articles made for Baal, Asherah, and all the host of heaven. And he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.

original.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְאֶת כֹּהֲנֵ֣י הַמִּשְׁנֶה֮ וְאֶת שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַסַּף֒ לְהוֹצִיא֙ מֵהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֣ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֗ים הָֽעֲשׂוּיִם֙ לַבַּ֣עַל וְלָֽאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה וּלְכֹ֖ל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיִּשְׂרְפֵ֞ם מִח֤וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בְּשַׁדְמ֣וֹת קִדְר֔וֹן וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵֽל

verses.restored: He removed the appointed idolatrous priests whom kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense at high places in cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations, and all host of heavens.

familiar.text: And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.

modern.text: Josiah also did away with the idolatrous priests ordained by the kings of Judah to burn incense on the high places of the cities of Judah and in the places all around Jerusalem—those who had burned incense to Baal, to the sun and moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.

original.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֣ית אֶת הַכְּמָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתְנוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְקַטֵּ֤ר בַּבָּמוֹת֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמְסִבֵּ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת הַֽמְקַטְּרִ֣ים לַבַּ֗עַל לַשֶּׁ֤מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֨חַ֙ וְלַמַּזָּל֔וֹת וּלְכֹ֖ל צְבָ֥א הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

verses.restored: He brought Asherah from house of YHWH outside Jerusalem to wadi Kidron, burned it at wadi Kidron, ground it to dust, and threw its dust upon graves of children of people.

familiar.text: And he brought out the grove from the house of the LORD, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people.

modern.text: He brought the Asherah pole from the house of the LORD to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem, and there he burned it, ground it to powder, and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.

original.text: וַיֹּצֵ֣א אֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָה֩ מִבֵּ֨ית יְהוָ֜ה מִח֤וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶל נַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֹתָ֛הּ בְּנַ֥חַל קִדְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֣דֶק לְעָפָ֑ר וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ֙ אֶת עֲפָרָ֔הּ עַל קֶ֖בֶר בְּנֵ֥י הָעָֽם

verses.restored: He tore down houses of qadesh by house of YHWH, where women were weaving houses/hangings for Asherah.

familiar.text: And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the LORD, where the women wove hangings for the grove.

modern.text: He also tore down the quarters of the male shrine prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women had woven tapestries for Asherah.

original.text: וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת בָּתֵּ֣י הַקְּדֵשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֗ים אֹרְג֥וֹת שָׁ֛ם בָּתִּ֖ים לָאֲשֵׁרָֽה

verses.restored: He brought all priests from cities of Judah and defiled high places where priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer-sheba. He tore down high places of gates at entrance of gate of Joshua governor of city, which were on left of a man at city gate.

familiar.text: And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city.

modern.text: Then Josiah brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and desecrated the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where the priests had burned incense. He tore down the high places of the gates at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which was to the left of the city gate.

original.text: וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת כָּל הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ מֵעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְטַמֵּ֣א אֶת הַבָּמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ שָׁ֨מָּה֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מִגֶּ֖בַע עַד בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וְנָתַ֞ץ אֶת בָּמ֣וֹת הַשְּׁעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ שַׂר הָעִ֔יר אֲשֶֽׁר עַל שְׂמֹ֥אול אִ֖ישׁ בְּשַׁ֥עַר הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: Only priests of high places did not go up to altar of YHWH in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.

familiar.text: Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

modern.text: Although the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, they ate unleavened bread with their fellow priests.

original.text: אַ֗ךְ לֹ֤א יַֽעֲלוּ֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֶל מִזְבַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֛י אִם אָכְל֥וּ מַצּ֖וֹת בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: He defiled Topheth in valley of sons of Hinnom, so no man would make his son or daughter pass through fire to Molech.

familiar.text: And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

modern.text: He also desecrated Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so that no one could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.

original.text: וְטִמֵּ֣א אֶת הַתֹּ֔פֶת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּגֵ֣י בני הִנֹּ֑ם לְבִלְתִּ֗י לְהַעֲבִ֨יר אִ֜ישׁ אֶת בְּנ֧וֹ וְאֶת בִּתּ֛וֹ בָּאֵ֖שׁ לַמֹּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: He removed horses kings of Judah had given to sun, from entrance of house of YHWH by chamber of Nathan-melech the court official in colonnades, and burned chariots of sun with fire.

familiar.text: And he took away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathanmelech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

modern.text: And he removed from the entrance to the house of the LORD the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun. They were in the court near the chamber of an official named Nathan-melech. And Josiah burned up the chariots of the sun.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁבֵּ֣ת אֶת הַסּוּסִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתְנוּ֩ מַלְכֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֤ה לַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ מִבֹּ֣א בֵית יְהוָ֔ה אֶל לִשְׁכַּת֙ נְתַן מֶ֣לֶךְ הַסָּרִ֔יס אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּפַּרְוָרִ֑ים וְאֶת מַרְכְּב֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Altars upon roof of upper room of Ahaz, which kings of Judah had made, and altars Manasseh made in two courts of house of YHWH, king broke down and ran from there, and threw their dust into wadi Kidron.

familiar.text: And the altars that were on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, did the king beat down, and brake them down from thence, and cast the dust of them into the brook Kidron.

modern.text: He pulled down the altars that the kings of Judah had set up on the roof near the upper chamber of Ahaz, and the altars that Manasseh had set up in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD. The king pulverized them there and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.

original.text: וְאֶֽת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַגָּג֩ עֲלִיַּ֨ת אָחָ֜ז אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֣וּ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶת הַֽמִּזְבְּחוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה בִּשְׁתֵּ֛י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיָּ֣רָץ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְהִשְׁלִ֥יךְ אֶת עֲפָרָ֖ם אֶל נַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: High places east of Jerusalem, south of Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel built for Ashtoreth deity of Sidonians, Chemosh deity of Moab, and Milcom deity of children of Ammon, king defiled.

familiar.text: And the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.

modern.text: The king also desecrated the high places east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of Corruption, which King Solomon of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

original.text: וְֽאֶת הַבָּמ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל פְּנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֮ מִימִ֣ין לְהַר הַמַּשְׁחִית֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּ֠נָה שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לְעַשְׁתֹּ֣רֶת שִׁקֻּ֣ץ צִידֹנִ֗ים וְלִכְמוֹשׁ֙ שִׁקֻּ֣ץ מוֹאָ֔ב וּלְמִלְכֹּ֖ם תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי עַמּ֑וֹן טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: He broke pillars, cut down Asherim, and filled their places with human bones.

familiar.text: And he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.

modern.text: He smashed the sacred pillars to pieces, cut down the Asherah poles, and covered the sites with human bones.

original.text: וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת הַמַּצֵּב֔וֹת וַיִּכְרֹ֖ת אֶת הָאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים וַיְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת מְקוֹמָ֖ם עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָֽם

verses.restored: Also altar at Bethel and high place Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made—both altar and high place he tore down. He burned high place, ground it to dust, and burned Asherah.

familiar.text: Moreover the altar that was at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, both that altar and the high place he brake down, and burned the high place, and stamped it small to powder, and burned the grove.

modern.text: He even pulled down the altar at Bethel, the high place set up by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin. Then he burned the high place, ground it to powder, and burned the Asherah pole.

original.text: וְגַ֨ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל הַבָּמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן נְבָט֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גַּ֣ם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֧חַ הַה֛וּא וְאֶת הַבָּמָ֖ה נָתָ֑ץ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֧ף אֶת הַבָּמָ֛ה הֵדַ֥ק לְעָפָ֖ר וְשָׂרַ֥ף אֲשֵׁרָֽה

verses.restored: Josiah turned and saw graves there in mountain. He sent, took bones from graves, and burned them upon altar, defiling it according to word of YHWH proclaimed by man of Divine who proclaimed these things.

familiar.text: And as Josiah turned himself, he spied the sepulchres that were there in the mount, and sent, and took the bones out of the sepulchres, and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it, according to the word of the LORD which the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these words.

modern.text: And as Josiah turned, he saw the tombs there on the hillside, and he sent someone to take the bones out of the tombs, and he burned them on the altar to defile it, according to the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these things.

original.text: וַיִּ֣פֶן יֹאשִׁיָּ֗הוּ וַיַּ֨רְא אֶת הַקְּבָרִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר שָׁם֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת הָֽעֲצָמוֹת֙ מִן הַקְּבָרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וַֽיְטַמְּאֵ֑הוּ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרָ֔א אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: He said, What is this marker I see? Men of city said to him, It is grave of man of Divine who came from Judah and proclaimed these things you did against altar of Bethel.

familiar.text: Then he said, What title is that that I see? And the men of the city told him, It is the sepulchre of the man of God, which came from Judah, and proclaimed these things that thou hast done against the altar of Bethel.

modern.text: Then the king asked, “What is this monument I see?” And the men of the city replied, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and pronounced these things that you have done to the altar of Bethel.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֚ה הַצִּיּ֣וּן הַלָּ֔ז אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֗יר הַקֶּ֤בֶר אִישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣א מִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתָ עַ֖ל הַמִּזְבַּ֥ח בֵּֽית אֵֽל

verses.restored: He said, Let him rest; let no man move his bones. So they let his bones escape, with bones of prophet who came from Samaria.

familiar.text: And he said, Let him alone; let no man move his bones. So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet that came out of Samaria.

modern.text: “Let him rest,” said Josiah. “Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” So they left his bones undisturbed, along with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַנִּ֣יחוּ ל֔וֹ אִ֖ישׁ אַל יָנַ֣ע עַצְמֹתָ֑יו וַֽיְמַלְּטוּ֙ עַצְמֹתָ֔יו אֵ֚ת עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר בָּ֖א מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: Josiah also removed all houses of high places in cities of Samaria, which kings of Israel had made to provoke, and did to them according to all deeds he did at Bethel.

familiar.text: And all the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, Josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in Bethel.

modern.text: Just as Josiah had done at Bethel, so also in the cities of Samaria he removed all the shrines of the high places set up by the kings of Israel who had provoked the LORD to anger.

original.text: וְגַם֩ אֶת כָּל בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְהַכְעִ֔יס הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּבֵֽית אֵֽל

verses.restored: He slaughtered all priests of high places who were there upon altars and burned human bones upon them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And he slew all the priests of the high places that were there upon the altars, and burned men’s bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

modern.text: On the altars he slaughtered all the priests of the high places, and he burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Jerusalem. Josiah Restores the Passover (2 Chronicles 35:1–19)

original.text: וַ֠יִּזְבַּח אֶת כָּל כֹּהֲנֵ֨י הַבָּמ֤וֹת אֲשֶׁר שָׁם֙ עַל הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת וַיִּשְׂרֹ֛ף אֶת עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּ֖שָׁב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: King commanded all people, saying, Make Passover to YHWH your Divine, as written in this scroll of covenant.

familiar.text: And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the LORD your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant.

modern.text: The king commanded all the people, “Keep the Passover of the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant.”

original.text: וַיְצַ֤ו הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת כָּל הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲשׂ֣וּ פֶ֔סַח לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם כַּכָּת֕וּב עַ֛ל סֵ֥פֶר הַבְּרִ֖ית הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: For such a Passover had not been made from days of judges who judged Israel, nor all days of kings of Israel and kings of Judah.

familiar.text: Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah;

modern.text: No such Passover had been observed from the days of the judges who had governed Israel through all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah.

original.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א נַֽעֲשָׂה֙ כַּפֶּ֣סַח הַזֶּ֔ה מִימֵי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣פְטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁפְט֖וּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכֹ֗ל יְמֵ֛י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: But in eighteenth year of king Josiah this Passover was made to YHWH in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: But in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the LORD in Jerusalem.

modern.text: But in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign, this Passover was observed to the LORD in Jerusalem.

original.text: כִּ֗י אִם בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ נַעֲשָׂ֞ה הַפֶּ֧סַח הַזֶּ֛ה לַיהוָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Also mediums, spirit-knowers, household gods, idols, and all detestable things seen in land of Judah and Jerusalem Josiah removed, to establish words of Torah written in scroll Hilkiah the priest found in house of YHWH.

familiar.text: Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and all the abominations that were spied in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, did Josiah put away, that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD.

modern.text: Furthermore, Josiah removed the mediums and spiritists, the household gods and idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem. He did this to carry out the words of the law written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.

original.text: וְגַ֣ם אֶת הָאֹב֣וֹת וְאֶת הַ֠יִּדְּעֹנִים וְאֶת הַתְּרָפִ֨ים וְאֶת הַגִּלֻּלִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל הַשִּׁקֻּצִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ לְ֠מַעַן הָקִ֞ים אֶת דִּבְרֵ֤י הַתּוֹרָה֙ הַכְּתֻבִ֣ים עַל הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָצָ֛א חִלְקִיָּ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Before him there was no king like him who turned to YHWH with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might, according to all Torah of Moses; and after him none arose like him.

familiar.text: And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the LORD with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.

modern.text: Neither before nor after Josiah was there any king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the Law of Moses.

original.text: וְכָמֹהוּ֩ לֹֽא הָיָ֨ה לְפָנָ֜יו מֶ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֤ב אֶל יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל לְבָב֤וֹ וּבְכָל נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וּבְכָל מְאֹד֔וֹ כְּכֹ֖ל תּוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְאַחֲרָ֖יו לֹֽא קָ֥ם כָּמֹֽהוּ

verses.restored: Yet YHWH did not turn from burning of his great anger, by which his anger burned against Judah because of all provocations by which Manasseh provoked him.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding the LORD turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn away from the fury of His burning anger, which was kindled against Judah because of all that Manasseh had done to provoke Him to anger.

original.text: אַ֣ךְ לֹֽא שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה מֵחֲר֤וֹן אַפּוֹ֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר חָרָ֥ה אַפּ֖וֹ בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה עַ֚ל כָּל הַכְּעָסִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְעִיס֖וֹ מְנַשֶּֽׁה

verses.restored: YHWH said, I will also remove Judah from before my face as I removed Israel; I will reject this city Jerusalem I chose and house of which I said, My name shall be there.

familiar.text: And the LORD said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.

modern.text: For the LORD had said, “I will remove Judah from My sight, just as I removed Israel. I will reject this city Jerusalem, which I chose, and the temple of which I said, ‘My Name shall be there.’” The Death of Josiah (2 Chronicles 35:20–24)

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה גַּ֤ם אֶת יְהוּדָה֙ אָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲסִרֹ֖תִי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּ֠מָאַסְתִּי אֶת הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֤את אֲשֶׁר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶת יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאֶת הַבַּ֔יִת אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתִּי יִהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Josiah and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Josiah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to king of Assyria at river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Neco put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.

familiar.text: In his days Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.

modern.text: At the end of Josiah’s reign, Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marched up to help the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went out to confront him, but Neco faced him and killed him at Megiddo.

original.text: בְּיָמָ֡יו עָלָה֩ פַרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֛יִם עַל מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר עַל נְהַר פְּרָ֑ת וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיְמִיתֵ֨הוּ֙ בִּמְגִדּ֔וֹ כִּרְאֹת֖וֹ אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: His servants carried him dead in chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his grave. People of land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.

familiar.text: And his servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own sepulchre. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father’s stead.

modern.text: From Megiddo his servants carried his body in a chariot, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father. Jehoahaz Succeeds Josiah (2 Chronicles 36:1–4)

original.text: וַיַּרְכִּבֻ֨הוּ עֲבָדָ֥יו מֵת֙ מִמְּגִדּ֔וֹ וַיְבִאֻ֨הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בִּקְבֻֽרָת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח עַם הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙ בֶּן יֹ֣אשִׁיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּמְשְׁח֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Twenty-three years old was Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

familiar.text: Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

modern.text: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah; she was from Libnah.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to all his fathers had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: Pharaoh Neco confined him at Riblah in land of Hamath so he would not reign in Jerusalem, and placed upon land tribute of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.

familiar.text: And Pharaohnechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.

modern.text: And Pharaoh Neco imprisoned Jehoahaz at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he could not reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed on Judah a levy of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

original.text: וַיַּאַסְרֵהוּ֩ פַרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֤ה בְרִבְלָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֔ת במלך בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּתֶּן עֹ֨נֶשׁ֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר כֶּ֖סֶף וְכִכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב

verses.restored: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz, who came to Egypt and died there.

familiar.text: And Pharaohnechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.

modern.text: Then Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and he changed Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz and carried him off to Egypt, where he died.

original.text: וַיַּמְלֵךְ֩ פַּרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֜ה אֶת אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֗הוּ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים וְאֶת יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז לָקָ֔ח וַיָּבֹ֥א מִצְרַ֖יִם וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Jehoiakim gave silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed land to give silver according to command of Pharaoh. From people of land, each according to his assessment, he exacted silver and gold to give to Pharaoh Neco.

familiar.text: And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxed the land to give the money according to the commandment of Pharaoh: he exacted the silver and the gold of the people of the land, of every one according to his taxation, to give it unto Pharaohnechoh.

modern.text: So Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh Neco, but to meet Pharaoh’s demand he taxed the land and exacted the silver and the gold from the people, each according to his wealth. Jehoiakim Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 36:5–8)

original.text: וְהַכֶּ֣סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֗ב נָתַ֤ן יְהוֹיָקִים֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֶעֱרִ֣יךְ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ לָתֵ֥ת אֶת הַכֶּ֖סֶף עַל פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה אִ֣ישׁ כְּעֶרְכּ֗וֹ נָגַ֞שׂ אֶת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְאֶת הַזָּהָב֙ אֶת עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ לָתֵ֖ת לְפַרְעֹ֥ה נְכֹֽה

verses.restored: Twenty-five years old was Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

familiar.text: Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.

modern.text: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah; she was from Rumah.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָ֨ה יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ זבידה בַת פְּדָיָ֖ה מִן רוּמָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to all his fathers had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו

translation_notes: Public reading and covenant renewal include elders, priests, prophets, and all people, but royal leadership and crowd participation do not guarantee free consent or ethically valid implementation.

Josiah's reform includes destruction, burning, defilement, and forced closure of other sacred practices. It is a major religious-violence text and may not authorize persecution, vandalism, desecration, or coerced conversion.

The Hebrew qadesh in verse 7 refers to a class of cult personnel and must not be rendered or weaponized as a generic slur against gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, queer, or gender-nonconforming people.
The women weaving for Asherah are skilled religious textile workers. Their labor and livelihoods must not disappear beneath the king's destruction of their workplace.

Topheth is disabled so children cannot be passed through fire. Preventing child sacrifice is ethically necessary, but child protection does not legitimate every violent act performed under the same reform.
Filling shrines with bones, opening graves, burning remains, and using corpses to defile altars are desecration of the dead. Prophetic fulfillment does not make grave violation good.
Josiah executes priests of high places without narrated trial. Religious office or belief never warrants summary killing.
Passover is Jewish covenantal practice. This account may not support Christian supersessionism, appropriation that erases Judaism, or coercion of Jews or others.
The removal of mediums and spirit-knowers may not support witch-hunts, occult panic, or violence toward contemporary spiritual practitioners.
Josiah is praised as unmatched in turning to YHWH, yet collective wrath remains. This exposes a morally troubling theology in which present reform does not spare later people from prior royal wrongs.
Huldah's promise that Josiah would be gathered in peace stands in tension with his death at Megiddo. The textual-theological tension must remain visible.

Egyptian power confines Jehoahaz, forcibly renames and installs Jehoiakim, imposes tribute, and drives taxation of the population. Puppet rule and imperial finance are central to the chapter's ending.
safety_note: Do not imitate Josiah's religious purge, target LGBTQ people through qadesh mistranslation, destroy sacred sites, desecrate graves, execute clergy or spiritual practitioners, or erase Jewish ownership of Passover. Preserve child protection, women's labor, bodily dignity, Huldah's unresolved oracle, and the population taxed and ruled beneath Egyptian imperial control.
